<reason>B won a close, high-quality clash by making the live choice easier: either the demand is already law and schooling, or it is an extra adult membership test attached by origin. A’s civic/language case and driver’s-test frame stayed competitive, but never named a native-adult analogue and overclaimed B’s classroom concession as a knockout. B’s equality and “gate, not heritage” line survived to the end; A’s two clipped turns added a small execution cost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s R2/closing on A’s Q2 concession: immigrant children already sit in the compulsory classroom, so leftover adult “adoption” is a second childhood no native adult faces—origin is the trigger, not the same bar.</best_rebuttal>
